extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, petitioners, patent owners, USPTO officials, and patent litigators
extracted.subtask_short: post-grant and inter partes review rules
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory rules (AIA) governing filing, institution, conduct, amendment, settlement, confidentiality, evidentiary standards, and appeals for inter partes reviews and post-grant reviews before the USPTO Patent Trial and Appeal Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing and confidentiality of settlement agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any agreement or understanding between the parties made in connection with, or in contemplation of, the termination of an inter partes review or post-grant review shall be in writing, and a true copy shall be filed in the Office before the termination of the review as between the parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the request of a party the agreement may be treated as business confidential information, kept separate from the patent file, and made available only to Federal Government agencies on written request or to any person on a showing of good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final written decision requirement (PTAB)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an inter partes review or a post-grant review is instituted and not dismissed, the Patent Trial and Appeal Board shall issue a final written decision with respect to the patentability of any patent claim challenged by the petitioner and any new claim added under the applicable amendment provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to all claims challenged and any new/amended claims proposed under the procedural rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate after final decision
rubrics_metrics.description: If the PTAB issues a final written decision and the time for appeal has expired or any appeal has terminated, the Director shall issue and publish a certificate canceling any claim finally determined to be unpatentable, confirming any claim determined to be patentable, and incorporating in the patent by operation of the certificate any new or amended claim determined to be patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificate effects claim cancellation/confirmation and incorporates new/amended claims into the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervening rights for amended/new claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposed amended or new claim determined to be patentable and incorporated into a patent following an inter partes or post-grant review shall have the same effect as that specified in section 252 for reissued patents regarding the rights of persons who made, purchased, used, or imported anything patented by such amended/new claim before issuance of the certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides protection for parties who acted before certificate issuance, analogous to reissue intervening rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public data on length of review
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office shall make available to the public data describing the length of time between the institution of, and the issuance of a final written decision for, each inter partes review and each post-grant review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to provide transparency about review timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to appeal PTAB final decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: A party dissatisfied with the final written decision of the PTAB under the applicable section may appeal the decision pursuant to sections 141 through 144. Any party to the review shall have the right to be a party to the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies appeals to the Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit for PTAB final written decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director to issue implementing regulations and possible institutional limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall, within 1 year after enactment, issue regulations to carry out the chapters governing inter partes and post-grant reviews. The Director may impose a limit on the number of reviews instituted during each of the first four 1-year periods if such number equals or exceeds a historical benchmark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations implement procedural details and the Director may manage initial workload by annual limits during transition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changed institution standard (inter partes reexamination context)
rubrics_metrics.description: Language changed from 'a substantial new question of patentability' to requiring that 'the information presented in the request shows that there is a reasonable likelihood that the requester would prevail with respect to at least 1 of the claims challenged in the request.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alters the threshold demonstrating whether a petition warrants institution (higher specificity about likely success on at least one claim).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file a post-grant review and fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to the chapter provisions, a person who is not the owner of a patent may file a petition to institute a post-grant review. The Director shall establish fees to be paid by the person requesting the review, in amounts the Director determines reasonable considering aggregate costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits third parties to challenge newly granted patents and requires fee-setting by the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of post-grant review grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner in a post-grant review may request to cancel as unpatentable one or more claims of a patent on any ground that could be raised under paragraph (2) or (3) of section 282(b) (relating to invalidity of the patent or any claim).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-grant review is broad in scope and can encompass many traditional invalidity grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-grant review filing deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for a post-grant review may only be filed not later than the date that is 9 months after the date of the grant of the patent or of the issuance of a reissue patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict 9-month window from grant or reissue issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition formal requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for post-grant review will be considered only if: (1) accompanied by payment of the Director-established fee; (2) identifies all real parties in interest; (3) identifies, in writing and with particularity, each claim challenged, the grounds on which the challenge is based, and the evidence supporting the grounds, including copies of patents/printed publications and affidavits/declarations if relying on other factual evidence or expert opinions; (4) provides other information as the Director may require; and (5) provides copies of required documents to the patent owner or its representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes particularity, evidentiary support, disclosure of real parties, fee payment, and service on patent owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: As soon as practicable after receipt of a post-grant review petition, the Director shall make the petition available to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions become public records subject to confidentiality redactions only if sealed motions accompany filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner's preliminary response right
rubrics_metrics.description: If a post-grant review petition is filed, the patent owner has the right to file a preliminary response within a time set by the Director that sets forth reasons why no post-grant review should be instituted based on failure to meet any requirement of the chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary response addresses threshold sufficiency of the petition rather than merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution threshold for post-grant review (more-likely-than-not)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may not authorize a post-grant review to be instituted unless the information presented in the petition, if not rebutted, would demonstrate that it is more likely than not that at least one of the claims challenged in the petition is unpatentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets a substantive 'more likely than not' burden for institution (higher than mere plausibility).

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution may be based on novel/unsettled legal question
rubrics_metrics.description: The institution determination may also be satisfied by a showing that the petition raises a novel or unsettled legal question that is important to other patents or patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows institution where the matter has broader legal importance even if unpatentability is not clearly more-likely-than-not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and notice of institution decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall determine whether to institute a post-grant review within 3 months after receiving a preliminary response or, if no preliminary response is filed, within 3 months after the last date such a response may be filed. The Director shall notify petitioner and patent owner in writing of the determination and make the notice public, including the date on which the review shall commence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 3-month statutory decision window and required written/public notice with commencement date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonappealability of institution decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director's determination whether to institute a post-grant review under this section shall be final and nonappealable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents interlocutory appeals from institution decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-grant review barred where pre-petition civil action exists
rubrics_metrics.description: A post-grant review may not be instituted if, before the date on which the petition is filed, the petitioner or real party in interest filed a civil action challenging validity of a claim of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents duplicative Office review where a civil action predates the petition filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic stay of civil actions filed after petition
rubrics_metrics.description: If the petitioner or real party in interest files a civil action challenging validity on or after the date the petitioner files a post-grant review petition, that civil action shall be automatically stayed until the patent owner moves to lift the stay, the patent owner files a civil action or counterclaim alleging infringement, or the petitioner moves to dismiss the civil action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automatic stay preserves Office proceedings as primary forum unless certain actions occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counterclaims do not constitute civil actions for bar
rubrics_metrics.description: A counterclaim challenging the validity of a claim of a patent does not constitute a civil action challenging the validity of a claim for purposes of the post-grant review bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes separate civil actions from counterclaims within existing litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary injunction consideration unaffected by filing of petition
rubrics_metrics.description: If a civil action alleging infringement is filed within 3 months after grant, the court may not stay consideration of the patent owner's motion for a preliminary injunction on the basis that a petition for post-grant review has been filed or instituted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects patent owner's access to preliminary injunctive relief shortly after grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joinder and consolidation of multiple petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: If more than one petition for a post-grant review is properly filed against the same patent and the Director determines more than one warrants institution, the Director may consolidate such reviews into a single post-grant review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows efficiency by consolidating overlapping petitions against same patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director discretion for multiple proceedings involving same patent
rubrics_metrics.description: During pendency of any post-grant review, if another proceeding or matter involving the patent is before the Office, the Director may determine the manner in which the post-grant review or other proceeding may proceed, including stay, transfer, consolidation, or termination. The Director may also reject petitions because the same or substantially the same prior art or arguments were previously presented to the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director may manage conflicts/duplication between Office proceedings to avoid redundant work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel from post-grant review final decisions (Office proceedings)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner in a post-grant review that results in a final written decision, or its real party in interest or privy, may not request or maintain a proceeding before the Office with respect to that claim on any ground that the petitioner raised or reasonably could have raised during that post-grant review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents repeated Office challenges to the same claim on the same or reasonably available grounds after final decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel in civil actions and ITC proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner in a post-grant review that results in a final written decision, or its real party in interest or privy, may not assert in a civil action under section 1338 or in an ITC section 337 proceeding that the claim is invalid on any ground that the petitioner raised or reasonably could have raised during that post-grant review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extends estoppel effect beyond the Office to certain litigation forums.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on post-grant review of reissue patents
rubrics_metrics.description: A post-grant review may not be instituted if the petition requests cancellation of a claim in a reissue patent that is identical to or narrower than a claim in the original patent, and the time limitations in section 321(c) would bar filing a petition for the original patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents circumvention of the 9-month filing window via reissue patents that narrow/duplicate original claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public file availability and sealing rules for proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations shall provide that the file of any proceeding under the chapter shall be made available to the public, except that any petition or document filed with the intent that it be sealed shall, if accompanied by a motion to seal, be treated as sealed pending the outcome of the ruling on the motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General rule of public access with a process for sealing confidential materials pending rulings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for showing sufficient grounds to institute
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations shall set forth the standards for the showing of sufficient grounds to institute a review under the institution provisions (e.g., the more-likely-than-not standard and the 'novel legal question' basis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director-prescribed standards implement statutory institution thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for submission of supplemental information
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations shall establish procedures for the submission of supplemental information after the petition is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows controlled supplementation of the petition record subject to regulatory rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery limited to directly related evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations shall set forth standards and procedures for discovery of relevant evidence, including that such discovery shall be limited to evidence directly related to factual assertions advanced by either party in the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrow discovery scope intended to focus on directly disputed factual assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions for abuse of discovery or process
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations shall prescribe sanctions for abuse of discovery, abuse of process, or other improper use of the proceeding, such as to harass or to cause unnecessary delay or unnecessary increase in cost of the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides deterrents against procedural misuse or harassment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protective orders for confidential information
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations shall provide for protective orders governing the exchange and submission of confidential information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables handling of confidential business information within the public proceedings framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner response after institution and supporting evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations shall provide for the filing by the patent owner of a response to the petition after a post-grant review has been instituted, and require that the patent owner file with such response, through affidavits or declarations, any additional factual evidence and expert opinions on which the patent owner relies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures the patent owner may present evidentiary support (affidavits/declarations) once review instituted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to amend standards and public disclosure of amendment-supporting information
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations shall set forth standards and procedures for allowing the patent owner to move to amend the patent to cancel a challenged claim or propose a reasonable number of substitute claims, and ensure that any information submitted by the patent owner in support of any amendment entered is made available to the public as part of the prosecution history of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows limited amendment while preserving public record of amendment-supporting materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to an oral hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations shall provide either party with the right to an oral hearing as part of the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves opportunity for oral argument within the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for final determination and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations shall require that the final determination in any post-grant review be issued not later than 1 year after the Director notices the institution of a proceeding, except the Director may, for good cause, extend the 1-year period by not more than 6 months and may adjust time periods in the case of joinder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory target for speedy resolution with limited extension authority for good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity for petitioner to file written comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations shall provide the petitioner with at least one opportunity to file written comments within a time period established by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures petitioner can comment on developments in the instituted review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's regulatory considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: In prescribing regulations, the Director shall consider the effect on the economy, the integrity of the patent system, the efficient administration of the Office, and the ability of the Office to timely complete proceedings instituted under the chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory design must balance systemic impacts, efficiency, and timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB conducts post-grant and inter partes reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Trial and Appeal Board shall, in accordance with section 6, conduct each post-grant review and inter partes review instituted under the chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Places responsibility for adjudication with the PTAB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner amendment options during review
rubrics_metrics.description: During a post-grant review the patent owner may file one motion to amend the patent to: (A) cancel any challenged claim; and/or (B) for each challenged claim, propose a reasonable number of substitute claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional motions may be permitted jointly to materially advance settlement or for good cause; however, amendments may not enlarge scope or introduce new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on enlarging scope or introducing new matter in amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment under the amendment provision may not enlarge the scope of the claims of the patent or introduce new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures amendments are narrowing/clarifying, not broadening or adding new subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary standard in post-grant review
rubrics_metrics.description: In a post-grant review instituted under the chapter, the petitioner shall have the burden of proving a proposition of unpatentability by a preponderance of the evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the standard of proof for merits determinations in post-grant review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement termination effects on estoppel
rubrics_metrics.description: A post-grant review shall be terminated with respect to any petitioner upon joint request of the petitioner and patent owner unless the Office has decided the merits before the request; if terminated with respect to a petitioner, no estoppel shall attach to that petitioner (or its real party in interest or privy) on the basis of that petitioner's institution of that post-grant review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement can avoid estoppel if termination occurs before the Office decides the merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to submit citations of prior art and owner written statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person at any time may cite to the Office patents or printed publications believed to have a bearing on patentability of any claim of a particular patent, or statements of the patent owner filed in a proceeding before a Federal court or the Office in which the patent owner took a position on claim scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides public ability to bring relevant prior art and owner statements to the Office's attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation becomes part of official file with explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: If the person citing prior art or written statements explains in writing the pertinence and manner of applying the prior art or written statements to at least one claim, the citation and explanation shall become part of the official file of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates a formal record in the patent file when pertinence is explained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to include related documents when submitting owner statements
rubrics_metrics.description: A party that submits a written statement pursuant to the owner-statement citation rule shall include any other documents, pleadings, or evidence from the proceeding in which the statement was filed that addresses the written statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures contextual materials accompany owner statements for completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on use of submitted written statements
rubrics_metrics.description: A written statement submitted pursuant to the owner-statement rule and additional information shall not be considered by the Office for any purpose other than to determine the proper meaning of a patent claim in a proceeding ordered or instituted pursuant to specified sections; if subject to a protective order, such information shall be redacted to exclude information subject to that order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restricts the Office's use of such materials to claim construction in specific proceedings and protects protected material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of identity of person citing prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon written request of the person citing prior art or written statements, that person's identity shall be excluded from the patent file and kept confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows anonymous submissions of prior art/citations subject to written request for identity protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB composition and appointment of administrative patent judges
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be in the Office a Patent Trial and Appeal Board constituted of the Director, Deputy Director, Commissioner for Patents, Commissioner for Trademarks, and administrative patent judges. Administrative patent judges shall be persons of competent legal knowledge and scientific ability appointed by the Secretary in consultation with the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the PTAB membership and qualification/appointment framework for administrative patent judges.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB duties
rubrics_metrics.description: The PTAB shall: (1) on written appeal of an applicant review adverse examiner decisions pursuant to section 134(a); (2) review appeals of reexaminations under section 134(b); (3) conduct derivation proceedings under section 135; and (4) conduct inter partes reviews and post-grant reviews pursuant to the applicable chapters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates core adjudicative responsibilities of the PTAB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-member panel hearing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each appeal, derivation proceeding, post-grant review, and inter partes review shall be heard by at least three members of the PTAB, designated by the Director. Only the PTAB may grant rehearings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates multi-member panels for specified adjudicative matters and centralizes rehearing authority in the PTAB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals to the Federal Circuit and procedural waivers
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant dissatisfied with a final decision in an appeal to the PTAB under section 134(a) may appeal to the United States Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit, and by filing such an appeal the applicant waives the right to proceed under section 145; similarly, parties to inter partes and post-grant reviews may appeal PTAB final written decisions only to the Federal Circuit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies appellate route (Federal Circuit) and statutory waiver consequences for certain appeal choices.
